I couldn't write the files because this request ruled out tools. Below are the complete contents for both files, ready to save as-is.

I kept all of your documentation, but I split it across two files. `SKILL.md` contains the operational content: the workflow, the type mapping and the output rules. Claude loads that file every time the skill triggers, so it stays lean. The Background and History sections and the closing line go verbatim into `reference/background.md`. Definitions of semver and git, and the story of how the process evolved, don't change what Claude does, and loading them on every run costs context without improving the output. Nothing was deleted.

I also filled a few gaps that would otherwise make Claude guess. These are clearly marked additions, not changes to your rules:
- What to do when the repo has no tags.
- How to find PR numbers and reverted commits, since `--oneline` alone hides commit bodies.
- How to resolve overlaps, such as a breaking change that is also security-related.
- What to do with commits that aren't conventional commits.

---

### `outputs/generating-release-notes/SKILL.md`

````markdown
---
name: generating-release-notes
description: Generates markdown release notes from git history using conventional-commit prefixes, writing RELEASE_NOTES.md at the repo root. Use when the user asks for release notes, a changelog for a release, or a summary of changes since the last tag.
---

# Generating Release Notes

Background on semver and git, and the history of this process, are in [reference/background.md](reference/background.md). You don't need them to run the workflow.

## How To Generate

1. Find the last release tag:
   ```bash
   git describe --tags --abbrev=0
   ```
   If this fails because the repo has no tags, ask the user which commit or range to use. Don't guess.

2. Collect the commits in that range:
   ```bash
   git log <tag>..HEAD --oneline
   ```
   `--oneline` hides commit bodies. Use the full log (`git log <tag>..HEAD`) when you need:
   - **PR numbers.** These are usually in the subject as `(#123)`. If they aren't there, check the body.
   - **Revert targets.** Look for `This reverts commit <sha>` in the body.

3. Group the commits by their conventional-commit type prefix. Each group becomes a section, as defined in the mapping below.

4. Write the result to `RELEASE_NOTES.md`, following the output rules.

## Commit Type Mapping

| Commit type | Section |
|---|---|
| `feat` | Features |
| `fix` | Bug Fixes |
| `perf` | Performance |
| `docs` | omit |
| `chore` | omit |
| `ci` | omit |
| `build` | omit |
| `refactor` | omit unless user-facing |
| `revert` | Reverts. Also remove the reverted entry if it is in the same release. |
| any type with `!` (e.g. `feat!`) | Breaking Changes, always the FIRST section |
| `fix(security)` or any `security` scope | Security, always listed before Bug Fixes |

When more than one row could apply, use this precedence:
- **Breaking first.** A `!` always wins, so `fix(security)!` goes under Breaking Changes.
- **Security second.** A `security` scope beats the plain type mapping.
- **Non-conventional commits.** If a commit has no recognizable type prefix, leave it out of the notes. List the skipped commits for the user so they can decide whether to include them.

## Output Rules

- Write the notes in markdown to `RELEASE_NOTES.md` at the repo root.
- Every entry links its PR number as `[#123]`. If a commit has no PR number, flag it to the user rather than inventing one.
- Entries are one line, in imperative mood, with no trailing period. Rewrite subjects as needed, e.g. `fix: fixed crash on login.` becomes `Fix crash on login`.
- Section order is:
  1. Breaking Changes
  2. Security
  3. Features
  4. Performance
  5. Bug Fixes
  6. Reverts
- Omit empty sections.

## Example output

```markdown
## Breaking Changes
- Remove deprecated `/v1/auth` endpoint [#412]

## Security
- Sanitize redirect URLs in OAuth callback [#418]

## Features
- Add CSV export to reports page [#405]

## Bug Fixes
- Fix timezone offset in scheduled jobs [#409]
```
````

### `outputs/generating-release-notes/reference/background.md`

```markdown
# Background and History

## Background

Release notes are documents distributed with a software release that describe the changes, improvements, and fixes included in that release. They help users and stakeholders understand what changed. Semantic versioning (semver) is a versioning scheme in which version numbers take the form MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, where MAJOR changes indicate breaking changes, MINOR changes indicate new backwards-compatible functionality, and PATCH changes indicate backwards-compatible bug fixes. Git is a distributed version control system that records changes to files over time; a git tag marks a specific point in history, typically a release.

## History of This Process

We used to write release notes by hand in Confluence, which took hours every sprint. In Q3 2025 we moved to a shell script that dumped raw git log output, but nobody could read it. In January 2026 Priya rewrote it around conventional commits, and in March we retired the old script after the mobile team migrated. This skill replaces all of that.

---

This tool is ABSOLUTELY AMAZING and will save your team HOURS of tedious work every single sprint!!!
```

---

If you'd rather keep everything in one file, you can append `background.md` to the end of `SKILL.md` and remove the link at the top. The skill will still work; it will just load extra text on every run.
